stdout: usage: bale pack [-h] [--context] [--slug SLUG] [--include PATH [PATH ...]]
[--write PATH [PATH ...]] [--exclude PATTERN [PATTERN ...]]
[--constraint TEXT] [--out-of-scope TEXT]
[--expects-probe {yes,no,claude-decides,agent-decides}]
[--readme-file PATH] [--checkpoint-file PATH] [--edit]
[--no-edit] [--no-readme] [--packer NAME]
[--work-class {code,doc,contract-doc,meta,mixed}]
[--supersedes SID] [--allow-checkpoint-in-scope]
[--no-include-group NAME] [--read-only] [--max-files N]
[--max-size BYTES] [--max-depth N] [--force] [--verbose]
[--json] [--dry-run]
[goal]
Build a request tarball and open its session. The goal is the ask; --include
selects what ships as context (default: the whole repo, minus .baleignore,
--exclude, and the built-in directory and secret-pattern filters); --write
declares the write forecast — the paths the session is expected to change,
which the concurrency gates read — or --read-only declares none. On a TTY,
omitting the goal or --slug enters the interactive wizard; piped, both are
required. Pack writes .bale/outbox/request-<sid>.tar.gz, and its report ends
with a paste-ready session opener for the worker's chat. --context instead
writes a session-less context tarball of the current directory's tree (no
session id, no session, no opener), to travel beside another project's request
as reading material. The flag surface's canonical description is TARBALL.md
positional arguments:
goal                  One-sentence goal for the session. Omit on a TTY to
enter the interactive wizard (BALE.md §7.3); required
when piped.
options:
-h, --help            show this help message and exit
--context             Write a session-less context tarball of the current
directory's tree instead of a request (v0.4.39;
BALE.md §7.8): .bale/outbox/context-<dir>.tar.gz under
the directory, holding the tree's files under one
<dir>/ folder, for attaching beside another project's
request as reading material. No session id is minted,
no session opens, no lock, telemetry, session log, or
opener; the read-only sweep does not run; outside a
git work tree it packs the tree as-is (no git-init
walkthrough). The pack filters still apply:
.baleignore, --exclude, the built-in directory and
secret-pattern filters, and the planner-bundle deny.
Composes with --include (paths inside the directory),
--exclude, --max-*, --force, --verbose, and --json;
every session-only flag (a goal, --slug, --write,
--read-only, --supersedes, --checkpoint-file, the
README flags, --constraint, --out-of-scope, --expects-
probe, --packer, --work-class, --allow-checkpoint-in-
scope, --no-include-group) refuses beside it.
--slug SLUG           Short kebab-case slug for the session ID. Omit on a
TTY to enter the interactive wizard; required when
piped.
--include PATH [PATH ...]
File or directory to include. Accepts multiple paths
per flag (e.g. --include src lib README.md) and is
itself repeatable; all paths flatten into one list.
Defaults to the whole repo if omitted.
--write PATH [PATH ...]
Declare the session's write forecast (ADR-0015): the
paths this session is expected to land changes under.
Same grammar as --include — accepts multiple paths per
flag, repeatable, directory entries cover their
subtrees — and entries must name existing paths
(forecasting the response's new-file layout is the
worker's job, ADR-0014; forecast the directory
instead). The forecast — not the include set — is what
the concurrency gates read: it is recorded in the
registry (sessions/<sid>/scope.json), stamped into the
manifest as resolved_scope, and enforced by the
disjointness, sibling-collision, and own-forecast
drift gates. It is a forecast, not a wall: out-of-
forecast work ships enumerated and is admitted per
path at apply. Absent --write, the forecast defaults
to the resolved include set — byte-for-byte pre-
separation behavior; separation is opt-in per pack.
Requires at least one path; the empty forecast is
spelled --read-only, and combining the two flags is
refused as contradictory.
--exclude PATTERN [PATTERN ...]
gitignore-style pattern to exclude from this pack.
Accepts multiple patterns per flag (e.g. --exclude
'data/*' 'tmp/*') and is itself repeatable. Composes
with .baleignore — these are session-only, .baleignore
is persistent (edit via `bale config init`). When the
wizard runs, omitting this flag triggers the
interactive 'anything to exclude' prompt; supplying it
skips that prompt.
--constraint TEXT     Add a constraint (repeatable). When the wizard runs,
omitting this flag triggers an interactive multi-line
prompt; supplying it skips that prompt.
--out-of-scope TEXT   Add an out-of-scope item (repeatable). Same wizard
interaction as --constraint.
--expects-probe {yes,no,claude-decides,agent-decides}
Whether the session expects a probe. The default,
agent-decides, has the worker probe whenever an
environment gap surfaces rather than guess around it
(TARBALL.md section 4.1); claude-decides is the same
posture under its pre-0.4.43 spelling, accepted for
good as an alias and stamped verbatim when typed.
--readme-file PATH    Read the request README's prose from PATH (UTF-8 text)
instead of the wizard's $EDITOR step — the non-
interactive way to ship prose context. A relative PATH
resolves like apply's tarball argument: cwd first,
then each configured apply.search_paths directory in
order (absolute paths bypass search; not-found names
every directory consulted). Fails loudly on a missing,
unreadable, or empty file (omit the flag to pack
without a README). Combines with --edit to review the
file in $EDITOR before packing.
--checkpoint-file PATH
Commit PATH's bytes as this session's per-sid blind
checkpoint and pack in the same invocation (v0.4.10) —
the one-command install retiring the two-run commit-
and-re-pack loop. A relative PATH resolves exactly
like --readme-file (cwd first, then each configured
apply.search_paths directory; absolute paths bypass
search); a missing, unreadable, or empty file fails
loudly. Requires a {sid}-bearing [validation] base:
bale peeks the sid, resolves the base against it,
commits the file's bytes at the resolved path as its
own commit on the current branch (subject naming the
sid), and proceeds. Idempotent: a resolved path
already committed with identical bytes proceeds (the
re-run of an aborted pack); differing bytes refuse —
the flag never silently replaces a ratified oracle. A
literal base refuses (commit the literal path
directly), an unconfigured base refuses rather than
ignoring the flag, and --read-only contradicts it at
arg-parse (the 0.4.9 waiver means there is nothing to
install). The checkpoint stays planner-authored: the
flag moves the planner's file into place; it does not
author one. On the wizard path a {sid}-based scoped
pack prompts for this path when the flag is absent
(typed flag skips the prompt).
--edit                Force the README $EDITOR step even when goal and
--slug are fully specified on the command line (where
the wizard never engages). Seeded with --readme-file's
content when given, with the standard scaffold
otherwise; saving an empty buffer omits the README.
Needs a TTY; conflicts with --no-edit.
--no-edit             In the wizard's README step, skip the y/N prompt and
$EDITOR entirely. Useful for non-interactive
automation that still wants the wizard to walk the
structured fields. Compatible with --readme-file (the
file's prose still ships — no editor opens); conflicts
with --edit. No-op on the fully specified path, which
has no $EDITOR step unless --edit asks for one.
--no-readme           Declare the pack deliberately ships no README prose.
Without it, a pack that resolves no prose warns on a
TTY and refuses when piped — an accidental prose-less
request should never look like a deliberate one. Skips
the wizard's README prompt (the flag is the answer);
conflicts with --readme-file and --edit.
--packer NAME         Packer identity stamped into the request manifest's
provenance block for this pack only. Precedence: this
flag > [identity].packer in <repo>/bale.toml > the
global bale.toml's [identity].packer (set either via
`bale config init`) > the literal 'unconfigured'
(logged with a hint).
--work-class {code,doc,contract-doc,meta,mixed}
Coarse class of the session's intended work, stamped
into the provenance block. Defaults to 'mixed' rather
than being required; the enum is a seed set — extend
via schema edit. On the wizard path the session-shape
question asks for it when this flag is absent
(v0.3.15); on the fully specified path omission still
stamps 'mixed', as before.
--supersedes SID      Declare this pack a split supersession of the named
session (v0.3.17): close SID as superseded-by-split —
after a y/N confirmation naming the cost (decline
default; piped stdin takes the decline without a
prompt, so a non-interactive supersession never closes
anything) — write its closure record (command 'pack'),
stamp depends_on.superseded_session in the new
request's manifest, and clear exactly that one
collision at the scope-disjointness gate; every other
open session still gates as usual. A SID that is not
open is accepted only when its telemetry history shows
a superseded-by-split closure (the idempotent re-run
of a supersession pack that aborted after the close);
anything else refuses. By contract this flag is
worker-authored only — it appears in worker-emitted
rescope commands (TARBALL.md §3.4) that the architect
pastes.
--allow-checkpoint-in-scope
Admit a pack whose resolved include set covers the
project's blind checkpoint path ([validation] base in
bale.toml), past the pack-time blindness refusal
(v0.3.28, board 6 session C; BALE.md §7.1 step 4b).
Without it, pack refuses such a scope: the checkpoint
is the planner's oracle, and a session shown or scoped
over its own oracle is the self-oracle shape the
refusal exists to close. The sanctioned ordinary
update path needs no session at all — the planner
edits and commits the checkpoint directly. Per-
invocation only, flag-only — deliberately no config
key, per the ratified override contract (a standing
opt-out is the rejected self-oracle-adjacent silent
bypass). Every use is logged prominently (FORCE: line)
and the admission is stamped into the request
manifest's provenance (checkpoint_scope_admitted), so
the session's telemetry carries it via the response's
provenance echo.
--no-include-group NAME
Opt this pack out of the project's configured include
group ([pack] include_group in bale.toml; board 64).
NAME must be the group's exact configured name — a
mismatch or an unconfigured group refuses, so a typo
cannot silently skip the pull. The opt-out is loud:
pack logs a FORCE line naming the group and the flag,
and the report carries an 'include group' row. Without
the flag, the group engages automatically whenever the
resolved includes touch a configured trigger path,
pulling the group's paths into shipped context (read
side only — the write forecast is never widened).
--read-only           Open the session with an EMPTY recorded write forecast
(v0.3.15; the degenerate forecast under ADR-0015): the
read-only session shape for discussion, orchestration,
or audit. The session opens normally in the registry —
sid, origin-branch stamp, lock — but its forecast
locks nothing (the ADR-0007 disjointness gates admit
sibling packs and applies alongside it) and may land
nothing (the own-scope drift gate refuses every
changes[] path a response under this sid ships; `bale
apply --allow-out-of-scope` can still admit named
paths deliberately, per invocation). --include still
selects what ships in context/ — a read-only session
reads files; it just cannot land changes to them.
--max-files N         Hard cap on file count (default: 100,000). Soft cap is
fixed at 10,000.
--max-size BYTES      Hard cap on total bundled bytes. Accepts a raw count
or a K/M/G suffix, e.g. '500M', '1G'. Default: 1.00
GB. Soft cap is fixed at 100.0 MB.
--max-depth N         Hard cap on path depth in directory levels (default:
--force               Bypass threshold caps AND the home-directory refusal.
The override is logged prominently to the session log.
Use for legitimate cases (dotfiles repo, deliberately
large pack); do not use to silence a soft-breach
prompt without thinking.
--verbose             Stream pack's quiet phases live (BALE.md §5.4): a per-
path line for every file the filter chain drops
(naming which filter — baked-in dir, secret pattern,
.baleignore/session exclude, outside --include) and
the tarball build trail (carried docs and tools,
manifest, README, each context copy, the tar step).
Hook output already streams live with or without the
flag. Walk lines run pre-session and reach the
terminal only; build lines also land in
.bale/logs/<sid>.log. Default output is unchanged.
--json                Emit the end-of-run pack report as one line of JSON on
stdout instead of the human summary block. Keys are a
stable contract for downstream tooling: outcome, sid,
tarball, log, session_dir, context_files. Packing
behavior, prompts, caps, and hooks are unchanged; json
mode's stream discipline sends the informational
'[bale] ' lines and any prompts to stderr, so stdout
carries exactly the JSON line on exit 0 (tail -n 1
recipes from v0.2.7 keep working).
--dry-run             Rehearse this line (v0.4.45): run every argv-only gate
against the live tree — flag pairs, the brief and
checkpoint reads, detached HEAD, the include group,
slug/goal, forecast existence, bundle-file naming, cap
values, checkpoint blindness, the supersession guards,
forecast disjointness — and stop. Exit 0 when every
gate passes, the refusing gate's own text otherwise.
Writes nothing: no session, lock, telemetry, tarball,
or closure; the supersession exchange and the read-
only sweep do not run, and a --supersedes parent stays
open. Refused beside --json and --context.
